descriptionAdvanced.en: Temuco is the bustling capital of the Araucanía Region and a primary hub for the indigenous Mapuche culture in Chile. Founded in 1881, it is a relatively young city that grew rapidly due to its role as a commercial center for agriculture and forestry. The city offers a unique blend of modern urban life and traditional indigenous heritage, which can be seen at the bustling Municipal Market. Temuco is surrounded by breathtaking natural beauty, including several national parks and volcanoes, making it a popular base for outdoor enthusiasts. The nearby Cerro Ñielol serves as a natural monument and a sacred site for the local Mapuche people.

en: The childhood home of Nobel laureate Pablo Neruda, who spent his formative years here.
Cerro Ñielol is the only natural monument in Chile located within an urban area.
A major center for Mapuche silverwork and traditional textile crafts.
The city's name means 'Temu water' in Mapudungun, referring to a native medicinal tree.
Hosts the Germán Becker Stadium, one of the premier sports venues in southern Chile.
